passage.title: What Makes an Effective Leader?
paras: We often picture leaders as loud, confident people who give orders. But the best leaders are judged not by how much power they hold, but by what they do with it.
First, an effective leader is honest. People follow a leader they can trust; once a leader is caught lying, every word they say afterwards is doubted.

Second, a good leader serves the people they lead. They listen, they share hardship, and they put the group's needs before their own comfort. A leader who eats well while others go hungry soon loses respect.
Third, a good leader is fair. They apply the same rules to friends and rivals, and they admit their mistakes instead of blaming others.
Finally, a good leader is accountable: they accept that others can question them, and they explain their decisions openly.
Muslims often recall the example of the Rightly Guided Caliphs, who were known for living simply and for inviting people to correct them. Leadership, in this view, is a trust (amanah), not a prize.

In Animal Farm, Orwell shows the opposite: a leader who rewrites the rules, silences questions and lives in comfort while others work. The warning is clear. Power without honesty, service and accountability turns into tyranny.
